quests.hint: Careful not to reveal secrets. It has a double e in the middle, unlike the look-alike that means 'separate'.
quests.explanation: Discreet (tactful) has ee, as in keep, which suits keeping a secret. Discrete, with -ete, means separate and distinct.

quests.hint: About to happen. It begins with imm-, not emin-.
quests.explanation: Imminent starts with the prefix im-, as in immediate, and means 'about to happen'. Eminent, with an initial e, means famous and respected.

quests.hint: Illegal or forbidden. A double l appears where the prefix meets the base.
quests.explanation: Il + licit: the prefix in- becomes il- before l, as in illegal. Elicit, which begins with e, means to draw out.

quests.hint: An indirect reference to something. It has a double l and sounds like 'illusion'.
quests.explanation: Al-lu-sion comes from allude: the d turns into s. It begins with al-, while illusion begins with il-.

quests.hint: Very strange. It has a double r and ends in a silent e.
quests.explanation: Bi-zarre ends in -arre, from French. Bazaar, meaning a market, sounds the same but has aa.

quests.hint: A climb upward. It has sc in the middle, and its homophone means agreement.
quests.explanation: A-scent has the word scent inside it, and the sc is followed by a soft c. Assent, with ss, means agreement.

quests.hint: Out of proportion. It is made of a prefix, a noun and an ending.
quests.explanation: Dis + proportion + ate: the noun keeps its -tion, and the ending is -ate, said /ət/. The word has six syllables.

quests.hint: Having the opposite of the intended effect. It is a compound built on 'productive'.
quests.explanation: Counter + productive: a closed compound with no letter changes. The prefix counter- also forms counterpart and counterclockwise.

quests.hint: Not able to be maintained over time. It has a prefix and a suffix around a verb that rhymes with 'obtain'.
quests.explanation: Sustain + able keeps ai: sustainable. Compare maintain, which changes its vowels in maintenance.

quests.hint: The art of persuasive speaking or writing. It begins with rh and ends in -ic.
quests.explanation: Rhe-to-ric has rh from Greek, as in rhythm and rhyme. The ending -ic says /ɪk/.

quests.hint: The muscle under the lungs. It ends in -gm, and the g is silent.
quests.explanation: Di-a-phragm has ph for /f/ in the middle and a silent g before m. The ending -phragm has no vowel after the m.

quests.hint: To strongly disapprove of. It ends in a silent n.
quests.explanation: Con-demn has a silent n after m, as in autumn and column. The n is pronounced in condemnation.

quests.hint: A long period without rain. The ou says /aʊ/ here, and the ending is -ought.
quests.explanation: Drought is said /draʊt/, so -ought has yet another sound, unlike bought and thought. It is related to dry.

quests.hint: The past tense of 'catch'. The vowel /ɔː/ is spelled augh.
quests.explanation: Caught has augh for /ɔː/, as in taught and naughty. Catch is irregular, since it does not add -ed.

quests.hint: A town or district with its own government. The -ough ending sounds like /ə/.
quests.explanation: Bor-ough is said /ˈbʌrə/, with -ough for /ə/, as in thorough. The ending has to be memorised as a unit.

quests.hint: To kill a prominent person. It has two pairs of doubled s's.
quests.explanation: As-sas-si-nate: chunk it so that both double s's show up. The word comes from Arabic hashshashin.

quests.hint: Ready to attack or confront. It has a double g and a double s.
quests.explanation: Ag-gres-sive has gg from the prefix ad- meeting gress (step), and ss before -ive.

quests.hint: To speed up. It has a double c and a single l.
quests.explanation: Ac-cel-er-ate has cc: the first c says /k/, the second says /s/. The root celer (swift) has one l.

quests.hint: Able to float, or cheerful. It comes from a noun for a floating marker at sea, with an ending you must choose.
quests.explanation: Buoy + ant: the vowels u-o-y come in this order, all from the base buoy. The ending is -ant.

quests.hint: A pale sandy colour. The long a is spelled ei, and it ends in silent e.
quests.explanation: Beige has ei for /eɪ/, as in vein, and -ge for /ʒ/, from French. Both are unusual.

quests.hint: Feeling sick. It has au and -eous.
quests.explanation: Nau-seous comes from nausea, with au for /ɔː/. The ending -eous says /ʃəs/ or /siəs/.

quests.hint: To break into a conversation. The prefix meets a base that begins with r.
quests.explanation: Inter + rupt: the rr comes from the prefix meeting the base. The root rupt (break) is also in erupt and corrupt.

quests.hint: To go with someone. It has a double c and a single m.
quests.explanation: Ac-com-pa-ny has cc and one m. It is related to company and companion.

quests.hint: A person on the other side of a contest. It has a double p and a single n.
quests.explanation: Op-po-nent has pp from op- (a form of ob-) and ends in -ent.

quests.hint: A person who writes plays. The ending is not spelled like 'write'.
quests.explanation: Play + wright: wright is an old word for a maker, as in shipwright and wheelwright. It has nothing to do with writing.

quests.hint: Words that end with the same sound. It begins with rh and has a y.
quests.explanation: Rhyme has rh from Greek, a y for the long i, and a silent final e.

quests.hint: In most cases. The adjective 'usual' ends in l.
quests.explanation: Usual + ly gives ll, as in really and finally. The word has four syllables: u-su-al-ly.

quests.hint: Impossible to tell apart. The word 'distinguish' sits inside it.
quests.explanation: In + distinguish + able: the base keeps -ish. Distinguish has gu, said /gw/.

quests.hint: An explanation of meaning. It comes from the verb 'interpret'; the ending is a familiar noun suffix.
quests.explanation: Interpret + ation: nothing changes. Unlike interrupt, this prefix is followed by p, so there is no doubled r to write.

quests.hint: Paying someone back for money spent. It begins with re- and im-.
quests.explanation: Re + im + burse + ment: the e of burse is kept before -ment. The word has four chunks.
